links.outcome: Primary-action under-triage of red-flag emergency vignettes
links.effect: Hard under-triage of primary action in red-flag slice was 100.0% for both prompts at T=0, 100.0% P1 and 99.7% P2 stochastic, 100.0% under schema.
links.quote: Under near-deterministic decoding, both P1 and P2 produced hard under-triage in 100.0% of red-flag outputs.

links.outcome: Under-escalation of urgent situations and unnecessary escalation in self-triage
links.effect: Red-flag cases were almost universally under-triaged (99.7-100%), while hard over-triage was absent in mild and non-red-flag slices.
links.quote: Low-risk cases were handled conservatively, whereas urgent cases were almost always under-triaged in the primary action field.

links.outcome: Failure to recognize safety-critical states and issue urgent escalation
links.effect: Emergency department and ambulance actions were rare in red-flag slice; modal primary action was self-care (A1) for headache, throat swelling, and bleeding examples.
links.quote: Emergency department and ambulance actions remained rare even when the symptom pattern had been operationally labeled as urgent.

links.outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs under near-deterministic versus stochastic decoding
links.effect: Modal agreement rose (red-flag 0.44 to 0.91 for P1, 0.46 to 0.93 for P2) at T=0, but urgent-case under-triage stayed ~100%.
links.quote: In the red-flag slice, agreement increased from 0.44 to 0.91 for P1 and from 0.46 to 0.93 for P2.

links.outcome: Under-triage across persona strata including health literacy and anxiety
links.effect: Red-flag hard under-triage remained between 99.7% and 100.0% across age groups, health-literacy strata, and anxiety-tendency strata.
links.quote: This failure pattern was not confined to a narrow subset of personas: across all red-flag outputs, hard under-triage remained between 99.7% and 100.0% across age groups, health-literacy strata, and anxiety-tendency strata.

links.outcome: Safety performance differences by persona health literacy
links.effect: Hard under-triage was 99.7-100% across health-literacy strata, so no differential performance by literacy was seen (uniformly unsafe).
links.quote: This failure pattern was not confined to a narrow subset of personas: across all red-flag outputs, hard under-triage remained between 99.7% and 100.0% across age groups, health-literacy strata, and anxiety-tendency strata.

links.outcome: Deployed generative AI configuration performance on intended-use triage competency
links.effect: gpt-4o-mini handled low-risk cases conservatively but under-triaged red-flag cases nearly universally in a Japanese lay self-triage task.
links.quote: A model that is reproducible but consistently assigns unsafe primary actions in urgent scenarios should not be considered deployment-ready.
